independence_statement: Saved before opening local spot, source, media or prior candidate records for these 25 names. External catalogues and search results were discovery aids only.
method_limits: Coordinates are approximate discovery points and do not prove a launch.
Rules count as resolved only when an authority or current operator identifies the relevant zone.
Image candidates are stored separately and none is approved by search relevance alone.
Full cloud/admin duplication access was unavailable; local comparison follows after hashing.

spots.name: Gott Bay, Tiree
spots.identity: Gott Bay by Scarinish, not Tiree as an island-wide aggregate.
spots.conditions: Broad, shallow and usually flat-to-choppy bay; strong wind can exceed forecasts.
spots.access_rules: Tides and rapidly changing Scottish conditions require local checks; exact launch zoning remains open.
spots.trip_value: Remote Hebridean setting and Tiree's wind-sports identity justify travel without proving world-class status.

spots.name: West Wittering
spots.identity: The Estate's marked 2XS water-sports area, excluding the swimming zone.
spots.conditions: Tidal sand-flat venue; high tide removes safe kite launch space.
spots.access_rules: Membership/sign-in applies; marked buoy zone, no high-tide launch, and 75 m separation from shore and swimmers.
spots.trip_value: Strong training, rescue and access infrastructure supports a dedicated trip, subject to unusually important operating rules.

spots.name: Llangennith
spots.identity: Llangennith/Rhossili beachbreak, with local peaks kept as one venue.
spots.conditions: Exposed 4.5 km west-facing beachbreak; east is offshore; rips intensify above roughly 4–6 ft.
spots.access_rules: Parking and schools exist; shipwrecks, tides and rips require explicit hazard copy.
spots.trip_value: Repeated national/international superlatives place it beyond the intended worth_trip tier.

spots.name: Daymer Bay
spots.identity: Daymer Bay inside the Camel estuary, not nearby Polzeath.
spots.conditions: Sheltered estuary sand venue; NW/N are favoured and currents strengthen around high tide.
spots.access_rules: Avoid about two hours around high tide; July–August daytime kite restriction reported and needs annual recheck.
spots.trip_value: Scenic estuary, beginner utility and Cornwall travel context support worth_trip once current rules are attached.

spots.name: Brandon Bay
spots.identity: Brandon Bay/Maharees wave cluster; individual reefs and beaches are subspots.
spots.conditions: Atlantic bay with reef and beach breaks; wind and waves can be much stronger than forecast.
spots.access_rules: National recreational-craft guidance applies; exact subspot, access and rescue data must be stored separately.
spots.trip_value: Longstanding international wave-windsurf reputation is too exceptional for the worth_trip tier.

spots.name: Keel / Trawmore, Achill
spots.identity: Trawmore/Keel beach on Achill, excluding Keem Bay.
spots.conditions: Three-kilometre exposed Atlantic strand; the eastern half has dangerous currents.
spots.access_rules: Summer lifeguards cover designated areas only; heed dangerous-current warning and national craft guidance.
spots.trip_value: Island landscape, several disciplines and schools make it a clear travel destination.

spots.name: Inch Strand
spots.identity: The five-kilometre Inch Strand on the Dingle Peninsula.
spots.conditions: Long exposed sandy strand with variable Atlantic beachbreak; conditions require daily local assessment.
spots.access_rules: Seasonal lifeguards and marked bathing areas take priority; current kite/wind zoning is not proven.
spots.trip_value: Length, scenery, school/hire and Dingle travel context support worth_trip for surfing.

spots.name: Strandhill
spots.identity: Strandhill beach and surf village, not the wider Sligo coast.
spots.conditions: Exposed beachbreak with permanent, unpredictable rips; not a swimming beach.
spots.access_rules: No swimming or paddling; surf only with appropriate ability and local guidance.
spots.trip_value: National Surf Centre and established surf-town services support worth_trip, but safety wording is mandatory.

sources.publisher: Where to Swim / Sligo Council references

spots.name: Hoddevik
spots.identity: Hoddevik bay at Stadlandet.
spots.conditions: Sheltered-by-mountains sandy bay, year-round surf; summer suits learners, larger swell brings rips and closeouts.
spots.access_rules: Cold-water preparation and local guidance are essential; parking is at the northern point.
spots.trip_value: Official tourism explicitly markets it as world-class and internationally attracting; exclude from worth_trip.

spots.name: Borestranda
spots.identity: Borestranda within Jærstrendene, not the entire Jæren coast.
spots.conditions: Long exposed sand beach with waves, current and cold water.
spots.access_rules: Kite is permitted at Bore, but bird-reserve seasonal restrictions and dune/camping bans must be mapped exactly.
spots.trip_value: Excellent access, facilities and Jæren landscape support worth_trip below the region-wide world-class boundary.

spots.name: Sola Beach
spots.identity: Solastranden authorized water-sports beach, not adjacent protected subareas.
spots.conditions: Accessible exposed Jæren beach with current, waves and stronger autumn conditions.
spots.access_rules: Kite is allowed at Sola; published bird-protection dates conflict (Oct vs Nov start) and require authoritative map/year resolution.
spots.trip_value: Airport access and strong water-sports use support worth_trip after the seasonal-rule conflict is resolved.

spots.name: Lomsesanden, Lista
spots.identity: Lomsesanden as the proposed Lista launch, not Lista as an aggregate.
spots.conditions: Popular south-coast sand venue; detailed wind window and hazards remain insufficiently sourced.
spots.access_rules: Parts of Listastrendene prohibit water sports; exact legal polygon for this launch is unresolved.
spots.trip_value: Lista has travel value, but acceptance must wait for a current official zone map.

spots.name: Thorlakshofn
spots.identity: Black-sand coast and Thorli surf area by Þorlákshöfn; exact current break footprint unresolved.
spots.conditions: Cold North Atlantic surf with powerful winter swells and volcanic-sand/reef setups.
spots.access_rules: Local knowledge, Arctic equipment and current harbour-construction status are essential.
spots.trip_value: Strong Icelandic surf identity is clear, but the break's current physical/status uncertainty blocks acceptance.

spots.name: Sandvik, Reykjanes
spots.identity: Sandvík beachbreak on Reykjanes; not similarly named Icelandic bays.
spots.conditions: Exposed black-sand beachbreak, SW–NW swell and east offshore; very cold, powerful and highly variable.
spots.access_rules: No current authority-backed access or rescue guidance was found; local guide and conditions check are mandatory.
spots.trip_value: Distinct scenery and surf potential exist, but evidence quality is not yet sufficient for publication.

spots.name: Toro Stenstrand
spots.identity: Torö Stenstrand in Ören nature reserve.
spots.conditions: Fickle open-Baltic wind swell over a cobble shore; autumn/winter are the main wave season.
spots.access_rules: Use marked parking and legal paths; do not cross private plots or disturb reserve habitat.
spots.trip_value: Sweden's best-known wave venue and unusual archipelago setting support worth_trip without global superlatives.

sources.publisher: Swedish Society for Nature Conservation, Nynäshamn

spots.name: Lomma Beach
spots.identity: Lomma northern beach water-sports area, excluding southern protected zones.
spots.conditions: Very shallow bay with broad standing area; popular with learners and Swedish windsurfers.
spots.access_rules: Kite/windsurf prohibitions apply in some reserves and the southern bay; launch must be pinned inside the recreation zone.
spots.trip_value: Access, club/hire and shallow-water character support worth_trip once the legal zone is attached.

spots.name: Yyteri
spots.identity: Yyteri surf centre/beach at Pori, excluding Munakari seasonal closure.
spots.conditions: Shallow sandy bay for learning; storms can produce roughly two-metre waves and advanced conditions.
spots.access_rules: Protect dunes; no camping on beach; Munakari access closed 1 April–31 July and boats excluded within 250 m of shore.
spots.trip_value: Multi-discipline centre, major dune landscape and rare Finnish wave potential support worth_trip.

spots.name: Tulliniemi Beach
spots.identity: Tulliniemi south beach water-sports section below the parking area, outside the swimming section.
spots.conditions: Windy dune beach; prime published wind range is north through southwest.
spots.access_rules: The first section below parking is reserved for swimmers; nature-area rules and exact sport entry need mapping.
spots.trip_value: Hanko scenery and established wind use support worth_trip after the launch/swim split is recorded.

spots.name: Ristna Beach
spots.identity: Ristna Beach at western Hiiumaa.
spots.conditions: Open Baltic exposure, coarse sand and rapidly deepening bottom; strongest waves commonly occur spring and autumn.
spots.access_rules: Experienced-user orientation is appropriate; no current formal launch zoning was found.
spots.trip_value: Hiiumaa journey, lighthouse landscape and Estonia-leading wave character support worth_trip.

spots.name: Parnu Beach
spots.identity: Pärnu central-beach designated surf area, not the entire bay.
spots.conditions: Shallow, warm-in-summer bay with urban surf clubs; conditions are generally flat to choppy.
spots.access_rules: During bathing season sailboards must remain in the surf zone; craft stay 25 m outside the marked bathing boundary.
spots.trip_value: City services and formal surf area support worth_trip after the exact zone geometry is stored.

spots.name: Pavilosta
spots.identity: Pāvilosta beach and Saka river-mouth area; exact discipline launches unresolved.
spots.conditions: Open Baltic coast and river mouth with seasonal wind waves.
spots.access_rules: Current launch, port-channel separation and protected-coast rules were not established from authoritative sources.
spots.trip_value: Town and coast have plausible travel value, but current primary evidence is too thin.

spots.name: Karosta Beach, Liepaja
spots.identity: Karosta beach at the end of Katedrāles Street, not Liepāja's central bathing beach.
spots.conditions: Wide exposed Baltic sand beach with strong wind and wind-wave potential.
spots.access_rules: Training/rental is documented; bathing zones, phosphorus hazard and protected-coast law require explicit guidance.
spots.trip_value: Unusual military-coast setting plus active centre and city services support worth_trip.

spots.name: Nida
spots.identity: Proposed Nida lagoon-side wind venue; Baltic beach and protected dune areas are separate.
spots.conditions: Windy Curonian Lagoon/sea setting with shallow-water potential but materially different sides.
spots.access_rules: National-park reserve boundaries are strict; exact legal launch and reported beach kite restrictions remain unresolved.
spots.trip_value: UNESCO landscape has exceptional trip value, but no publishable launch identity is yet proven.

spots.name: Kintai
spots.identity: Kintai Beach launch on the mainland Curonian Lagoon shore.
spots.conditions: Shallow sandy shore with flat-to-choppy water and prevailing W-sector winds; reeds and weed are hazards.
spots.access_rules: Use the established beach rather than the small/deeper observation-tower entry; current nature-season rules need recheck.
spots.trip_value: Accessible lagoon flat water, instruction and nearby delta/Curonian travel context support worth_trip.

spots.name: Sventoji
spots.identity: Šventoji Baltic beach kite area shown in the Palanga visitor map.
spots.conditions: Open Baltic beach; detailed wind window, bottom and hazards were not independently verified.
spots.access_rules: A kite location is mapped, but current beach-season zoning and exact launch boundaries remain unverified.
spots.trip_value: Resort context is plausible, but evidence is insufficient to distinguish a trip-worthy spot from a local launch.
